title: Start here
intro: Where to start when you are in front of a target and need the next command, not a tutorial. Pick your situation, open it, and jump straight to the moves and the tool that does the work. Search filters every play. This is a working reference for authorised testing only.

groups.name: A port is open
groups.blurb: Straight off the scan: the first move on each service, then the route to access.

scenarios.label: SMB (445 / 139)
scenarios.detail: The richest target on a Windows network. Enumerate anonymously, then with a credential.

steps.text: Null / guest session: shares, users, groups and the password policy in one pass.
With a credential: spray, list shares, look for (Pwn3d!) and dump.
Local admin? Execute, or relay unsigned SMB.

scenarios.label: HTTP / HTTPS (80 / 443 / 8080)
scenarios.detail: Fingerprint the stack, discover content, then attack the app.

steps.text: Identify the stack and find hidden content and vhosts.
Put a proxy in front so you can read and replay every request.
Test the inputs: SQLi, LFI, upload, command injection, SSTI.
Known off-the-shelf app (WordPress, Tomcat, Jenkins, GitLab)?

scenarios.label: FTP (21)
scenarios.detail: Anonymous first, then a login, then what the login lets you do.

steps.text: Try anonymous, list and pull files.
Brute a real login with a short list; writable root under a web dir = webshell upload.

scenarios.label: SSH (22)
scenarios.detail: Keys and weak passwords are the way in.

steps.text: Throttle to ~4 tasks and brute a known or likely user.
Found an id_rsa? Crack it if encrypted, then log in.

scenarios.label: RDP (3389)
scenarios.detail: A full desktop with a credential or a hash.

steps.text: Brute (keep -t low), or connect with a credential.
Only have the hash? Pass it (needs Restricted Admin).

scenarios.label: MSSQL (1433) / MySQL (3306)
scenarios.detail: A database login is often command execution.

steps.text: Log in, enable and run xp_cmdshell on MSSQL.
Capture the service's NetNTLM hash with a UNC path, then crack/relay.

scenarios.label: SNMP (161/udp)
scenarios.detail: Community strings leak the whole config.

steps.text: Guess the community string, then walk it for users, processes and secrets.

scenarios.label: DNS (53)
scenarios.detail: A zone transfer hands you the namespace.

steps.text: Try a zone transfer, then brute subdomains.

groups.name: I have a shell
groups.blurb: First execution on a host. Stabilise, enumerate, escalate.

scenarios.label: The shell is unstable
scenarios.detail: No job control, dies on Ctrl-C.

steps.text: Upgrade to a full PTY.
cmd: # Ctrl-Z; stty raw -echo; fg; export TERM=xterm

scenarios.label: A Windows shell
scenarios.detail: Enumerate the host and your token, then escalate to SYSTEM.

steps.text: Who am I, what privileges, what is running.
Run a scanner, then exploit the one finding (services, tokens, AlwaysInstallElevated).
Dump the local credential stores.
cmd: reg save hklm\sam sam.save & reg save hklm\system system.save

scenarios.label: A Linux shell
scenarios.detail: Enumerate, walk the privesc primitives, get to root.

steps.text: Context and the quick wins.
Run linPEAS, cross-check SUID/sudo on GTFOBins.
Hunt for credentials in configs, history and keys.

groups.name: I have credentials or a hash
groups.blurb: Turn a secret into access, or into a password.

scenarios.label: A plaintext password
scenarios.detail: Spray it, reuse it, log in with it.

steps.text: Spray across the subnet for reuse, then get a shell.

scenarios.label: An NTLM hash
scenarios.detail: Authenticate with the hash, no cracking needed.

steps.text: Pass the hash over SMB / WinRM, or spray it.

scenarios.label: A Kerberos ticket or keytab
scenarios.detail: Reuse a ccache/keytab, or extract the hash from it.

steps.text: Point tools at the ccache, or import a keytab.

scenarios.label: A captured hash
scenarios.detail: Identify the type, then crack it.

steps.text: Name the format, then wordlist + rules.

scenarios.label: A protected file (zip / kdbx / office)
scenarios.detail: Extract a crackable hash with a *2john tool.

steps.text: Convert, then crack.

groups.name: I'm attacking Active Directory
groups.blurb: The domain: from no creds to Domain Admin.

scenarios.label: On the internal network, no credentials
scenarios.detail: Poison, relay and name the domain.

steps.text: Poison LLMNR/NBT-NS to capture NetNTLMv2 hashes.
Relay that auth to an unsigned host instead of cracking.
Find the domain and enumerate users for a spray.

scenarios.label: I have a domain credential
scenarios.detail: Map the domain and find the path.

steps.text: Collect BloodHound data and read the shortest path to DA.
cmd: bloodhound-python -u user -p pass -d domain.local -c all -ns TARGET

steps.text: Roast: Kerberoast service accounts and AS-REP roast pre-auth-less users.

scenarios.label: I need to move to another host
scenarios.detail: Pass what you have: hash, key, ticket or certificate.

steps.text: Pick the technique for what you hold.
cmd: # hash -> Pass-the-Hash; key -> OverPass-the-Hash; cert -> PKINIT; ticket -> Pass-the-Ticket

scenarios.label: I have Domain Admin
scenarios.detail: Dump everything and prove it.

steps.text: DCSync or dump NTDS.dit for every domain hash.
cmd: netexec smb DC -u user -p pass -M ntdsutil
